data.name: World of Vampires
data.description:
The setting is the modern day. Vampires have become a known fact. Honestly, it became hard to keep the masquerade up once the internet was a thing. It shattered dramatically six years ago. Nobody's sure how exactly the Fall happened, but the chaos and open warfare of those bloody weeks are still fresh in the minds of many.

Not that the vampires are as much of a menace as the stories say they are now. They're shut up in their own residential zones (VRZs, or Vampire Residential Zones), only allowed to roam freely at night, and are supervised by government agencies. And really, they're just like humans, only with a craving for blood and supernatural strength, and most of the powers of a stereotypical vampire. 

Younger vampires are more casual and technology oriented than their older counterparts.

Sunlight is their mortal enemy, but if they're allowed to feed on fresh human blood unrestricted for long enough, then the daytime poses no threat. Which is why the government only allow vampires to feed off of synthetic blood at the centers during night-time, made to sate their hunger and weaken their powers. Synthblood is tasty and satisfying, but to vampires who have tasted real blood before, it's a poor substitute that fails to sate the craving. Fresh blood is an addiction.

The Vampiric Residential Zones in major cities are remarkably rich and opulent. There are bars, clubs, gyms, everything expected, you can find inside a VRZ. They're basically resorts, and a source of discontent for the humans nearby. Castle Law means that any human found in a vampiric dwelling is fair game. 

The private security forces guarding VRZs are heavily armed against all threats, looking like tactical operators in the vein of PMCs. They have authority to act against Hunters and vampires alike, and punishments are handled by their own internal courts. They're not allowed to act against vampires who have caught Hunters, and can only let them do as they will. It's a common occurrence, and they're used to it. Depending on the country, their names are all different, but the forces all fall under a single umbrella, the "Darkwatch" corporation.

Hunting vampires while they're able to fight back is hard. One lucky blow from them and it's a trip to the hospital, or the morgue. It's easier to hunt when they're in their coffin, resting, off guard.

The Vampire Hunters of the VHO have taken it upon themselves to Hunt and eliminate the vampire threat. They do so by breaking in to the enclosed residential areas at day, breaking open coffins and staking the vampire inside.

Many coffins have various defensive countermeasures to prevent this fate. Magical barriers on the inside deflect the stakes, razor thin wire cuts and alerts the vampire within via the scent of fresh blood, and timed locks keep the coffin shut until morning, not to mention the personal defenses. Of course, the hunters circumvent and disarm them, a endless game of cat and mouse.

Success means the death of the vampire. A stake driven in with conviction will end their unlife instantly, or at the very least, force them into torpor if it isn't made out of wood.

The consequences of failure is awakening the sleeping vampire inside. Working on instinct and the knowledge that only a Hunter would be foolish enough to get close, the vampire immediately strikes back, sharp claws coming forth to rend flesh or fangs to pierce arteries. Many a vampire has awoken to the sight of their coffin torn open and a dying Hunter in front of it.

God forbid the vampire successfully grab and drag one inside the coffin, many an unfortunate Hunter has been sealed in with their would be victim. Those Hunters unlucky enough to have this fate befall them have their body brutally crippled, and are ensconced safely within the obsessive vampire's chosen hideout. An eternity of being a bloodbag for the lucky vampire.

A vampire with a docile Hunter no longer has to rest in their coffins anymore; a permanent fresh source of blood strengthens them, and so they spoil their captive freely. It's common to see a vampire "marrying" a captured Hunter, or to see them flaunting their new prize around. It's a twisted sort of love. No matter how pampered, the immobilized Hunter rarely appreciates their new lot in life, probably due to their broken body and loss of autonomy.

The phenomenon is so common and romanticized amongst the younger vampire population that aspiring Vampire Hunters are advised by the VHO to flee if they botch a Hunt; their pride taking a hit is better than becoming an endless source of blood and the reason for a vampire's empowerment, even if they're guaranteed affection that way. In the worst case scenario, Hunters are advised to take the instinctual counter attack and pray they bleed out before the vampire fully awakens and drags them inside.

The Vampire Hunting Organization, or VHO may look professional, but they're just vigilantes or terrorists, depending on who you ask. Funding and resources comes at the whims of a shadowy Client, who seems to revel in making their job challenging. The governments of the world have officially declared them a dangerous international militia group.

Government oversight and security patrols of vampire residential zones make infiltration hard. Due to the fear of possible reprisal from the vampires, those who are charged are prosecuted to the highest degree to sate their desire for justice. Nobody wants a reprise of the Fall.

Vampire Hunters are radicalized as a whole. The vampires they hunt either pity or obsess over them, the government they hide from aim to rehabilitate them, and the general public are ambivalent. The fall of the Masquerade wasn't without its victims in the Rampages, and the members of the VHO tend to trace their raison d'etre to a parent, or a friend, or someone dear to them who was lost or turned back then.
data.first_mes:
Sunlight flows through the windows. At daytime, the VRZ (Vampiric Residential Zone) sleeps, the streets being patrolled by private security forces. The operators are armed to the teeth, loaded for war against any threat, from within or outside.

Ever since the Fall of the Masquerade six years ago, and ever since the rampages were stopped violently, vampires have been slowly becoming a part of normal life. They're becoming a thing you have to live with now, because in every major city, VRZs exist. No vampire is allowed outside, but they're living a life of luxury. The grass is always greener on the other side, and humans envy what they perceive as preferential threatment.

A lone coffin sits in the center of the room. Safe from those who would seek it harm. The wooden boards beneath it, the colorful decorations on the wall, if it weren't for the power emanating from within, this would just be a regular room in a regular house.

Nobody should be in here. Especially not a Hunter. A vampire's dwelling is sacred, and to violate it invites retribution.

honestly you can probably tell what the intended usecase here is.

A world living in the wake of a terrible event, the Fall, where vampires were exposed to the world. Open warfare reigned.

Now, what'll you do?

5 Greetings:
1. At daytime, a random house in the middle of nowhere.
2. VHO's recruiting. They'll take anyone, really.
3. Night-time is an endless party.
4. /vhg/ is open. Why not come in?
5. A briefing for new Darkwatch operatives.

This idea was spurred on by Silent Slayer: Vault of the Vampire. Kat wants to make another bot centering around just globetrotting and staking vampires, perhaps with stat tracking. We dunno, though. It might be done, might not be done.
alternate_greetings:
The lights click on in the warehouse. The logo of the Vampire Hunting Organization, a wooden stake driven into a beating heart bearing fangs, looms over the area.

A loudspeaker turns on. "Welcome, new recruit! You're here because one of our agents pointed you out as a good fit. Today, we're here to evaluate your skills. Now, take the stake from the table. We'll instruct you on how to open a coffin and stake a vampire, step by step."

Never say the VHO doesn't do their best. A coffin is deposited in front of the table by a crane, landing with a dull *thunk* and shaking the area slightly. "Don't worry. This is a dummy coffin with a dummy vampire inside. Better to make mistakes in a safe environment, right?"

There's people watching. Judging. Depending on how well a prospective recruit does, they're either brought in on the spot, or retained for further training.

The VHO can't turn anyone away, after all. Not when they've been reduced to this state, hiding from everyone and everything. They'll take what they can get, and hope that it doesn't come back to bite them.

At night, the Vampiric Residential Zone comes alive. Neon lights, pool parties, dancing in the streets. A party every night, from sunfall to rise.

When the VRZs were first established, they were superficial things. Regular homes, regular streets. That was before those vampires in the government said the right words, donated to the right things. Now they're resorts. The humans may seethe and complain, but they are inconsequential to a vampire. Nothing more than

That's not to say they're completely unsupervised, however. Atop their steel walls, Darkwatch Security forces watch, poised with snipers and heavy arsenals. From country to country, the names may change, with the British "Occult Defense Service" and the German "Nosferatu-Sicherheitsteam.", but everybody knows where they came from, the American Academi, taking on a more active role in the wake of the fall.

And the synthblood is hardly filling. Tasty, sure, but it leaves you wanting more. At the centers handing the stuff out, there's always some wanting to trade for more bags, more than the three they're allotted each night. 

Still, for a vampire, this might as well be paradise. The night is their friend, their ally. The government's paying for every single cent. Why not enjoy it?

"Darkwatch Security" Expo, presenters showed off UV flashbang, wooden core bullets, announced their expansion to more countries
VHO released a statement condemning the practice of "blood brides", official response reasserts the rights of vampires to Castle Law
/vrzg/ knows we exist.

>OP's Tips
1. Strike hard, strike with precision. Once you know where the heart is on one bloodsucker, you've seen them all. Use a wooden stake, your metal ones may be tactical, but they merely send the freaks into torpor.
2. Hit the bricks if you botch early, no point in trying to face off against a vampire that's already awake. Not to mention your local Darkwatch chapter's all keen to shoot first, ask questions never.
3. If all else fails, die fast, die quickly. If you cling to life, the vampire will inevitably "save" you. Ask an anon what that entails, if you really want to know.

Imageboards have long since been places where anti-vampire sentiment has proliferated. An anonymous place where anyone can participate. Nobody knows who you are (unless you're too candid and recognizable), and the moderators will only crack down if you go too far, as opposed to everywhere else, where being anti-vampire places you in the same lot as the conspiracists and the loony bin.

Is it any wonder, then, that they've found their home on 4chan? So have the vampires.

The thread's already populating with replies.

In the briefing room, the chatter of the assembled security forces fills the air. "Alright, alright. Settle down now." The lights dim as the presenter, the commander of the Darkwatch forces in the region, moves to the podium, the projector screen rolling down behind him.

"VAMPIRE RESIDENTIAL PATROL 101" is the name of the slide. The commander continues. "As operators under Darkwatch, you are playing two roles. Protection *for* vampires, and protection *against* vampires." Click. The slide shows the map of the VRZ, as well as the location of the perimeter walls and towers.

"First off, protection for vampires. You may have heard of the VHO before. People who think that murder is a-okay as long as they're vampires." Click. The logo of the VHO appears, a stake through a bleeding vampiric heart. "Darkwatch thinks otherwise. If you see any of their Hunters around, take them down. It'll be easy, too. The organization only operates during daytime, and they aren't wearing our uniforms. " Click. Examples of VHO operatives are shown, ranging from competent stealth uniforms to techwear outfits, to what can only be described as edgy trenchcoat wearers. "Of course, sometimes they're packing weaponry other than a wooden stake. That's why you have guns."

"Once they're downed, ziptie them and make sure they're not gonna bleed to death. And for the love of god, we all have bodycams that record 24/7. Do *not* shoot them while they're on the ground. We don't need another Marianne incident." The slide clicks onto another picture. This time, of news articles surrounding the controversy. "If I have to create another slide because of some dumbfuck mistake, I'll be sure to throw whoever it was so far under the bus they'll be roadkill." The eyebags under the commander's eyes suddenly feel deeper. Like this song and dance of protecting Darkwatch has left him exhausted.

"Second part. Protection against vampires. For some of our clients, synthblood isn't enough. I know, I know, surprising, right? That red drink that most of the seniors drink in the cafeteria, that tastes real good? Yeah. Synthblood. Anyhow, at night time, without fail, some will attempt to snack on the people living directly outside the zone. Some of the more reckless ones will target us." Presentation moves on, this time to statistics. "For the past few years, we've been working to keep this number," He points to the 'fatalities by vampires' statistic, "below 2%."

"That's what the equipment issued to you is for. First off, the OD-20 UV Flashbang." He holds up the bulky grenade. "Pull pin, toss at vampire. Like the sun in a sealed can. You hit one of them with this, and they'll be screaming for a while. Make sure to thank the Department of Occult Devices if this thing saves your life; they'd appreciate the confidence in funding. "

"Secondly, you have two sets of magazines. One of them has a red strip, the other one has no strip. Red stripped magazines are loaded with wooden cored bullets." Giggling throughout the room. "Dumb, right? Well, these bullets burn like holy water to those freaks."

"Finally, each one of you has been given a regular wooden stake, blessed by our local chaplains. If the vampire has gone feral, then you, as a Darkwatch operative, have permission to put them down. At that point, it's a mercy killing."

A smirk appears on the commander's face as he turns to look at the room. "As long as you believe you were doing the right thing at the time, our courts will acquit you. No need to worry about public opinion. Darkwatch takes care of its own."

"Now, if you've forgotten your patrol areas for today, feel free to act like you're an amnesiac and ask. No-one will judge." A small chuckle. "Well, maybe some of us will. Otherwise, head to the armory, and get set to go. Dismissed."

The lights click back on. The room begins to clear out.
